newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: EU opposes Slovak-Russian free trade area - Meciar.
newsitem.headline: EU opposes Slovak-Russian free trade area - Meciar.

text.p: Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said on Thursday that the European Union opposed creating a free trade area between Slovakia and Russia, an idea Bratislava has considered in the past year.

"The countries of the EU have pointed out to us that any steps towards liberalisation of trade with Russia...no matter how advantageous...would have negative political signals on Slovakia's foreign political orientation," Meciar told a meeting of leading Slovak industrialists.

Slovak leaders including Meciar have frequently raised the possibility of such a free trade area, provoking opposition accusations that Bratislava was looking to its old allies in the East despite officially following a pro-Western line.

Meciar said a second reason for a negative EU attitude on closer Slovak economic ties with Russia was that if Slovakia joined the EU, the Union would have to compensate for breaking an eventual free trade agreement with Russia.
Slovakia, an associate member of the EU, formally applied for EU membership last year.
"We said this need not be an obstacle because we could conclude agreements with Russia valid for one or two years and extend them by one year and terminate them as the situation arises," Meciar said.
"It is a matter of political will and economic consideration (of the EU) to either support or not support such steps," he added.

The premier said the need to reassess Slovakia's economic relations with Russia were caused by the country's soaring trade deficit with Moscow, Slovakia's sole oil and natural gas supplier and major raw materials source.
Of Slovakia's total foreign trade deficit of 35 billion slovak crowns ($1.12 billion) in first eight months of this year, 30 billion crowns was on trade with Russia.
